extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: Video-MME is the first-ever comprehensive Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis. It consists of 900 videos across 6 primary visual domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Artistic Performance, Life Record, and Multilingual) with 30 fine-grained subfields, annotated with 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice questions (3 per video). Videos range in duration from 11 seconds to 1 hour, covering short-, medium-, and long-term videos. The benchmark integrates multi-modal inputs including video frames, subtitles, and audios.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.publisher: Nanjing University, State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, XMU, HKU, PKU, CUHK, ECNU, CASIA
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The construction of the Video-MME dataset involves three main steps: video collection, question-answer annotation, and quality review. Raw videos were sourced from YouTube based on a domain hierarchy of 6 key domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Artistic Performance, Life Record, and Multilingual) with 30 fine-grained subcategories. Videos were collected with varying duration lengths including short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long videos (30-60 minutes), along with corresponding meta-information such as subtitles (if provided) and audios.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Out of 900 videos, 744 videos have subtitles and all 900 have audios, indicating that 156 videos are without subtitles.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos were sourced from YouTube, informed by popular trends on YouTube. Associated subtitles (if provided) and audio tracks were also obtained.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions that could be answered solely based on textual questions (without video content) were filtered out by providing text-only questions to Gemini 1.5 Pro. Questions that did not meet this criterion were returned to the original annotator for revision. Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup, confirming the robustness of the video content-based requirement.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning were recruited. Each annotator was tasked with thoroughly viewing the entire video, then iteratively creating three relevant questions, each accompanied by four candidate options, contributing to a total of 2,700 QA pairs. A multiple-choice QA format was used. The questions encompass 12 distinct task types including perception, reasoning, and information synthesis. Each QA pair is designed to be closely tied to the video content. A rigorous manual review process was conducted where each QA pair underwent examination by a different annotator to verify clarity, answerability, and appropriateness of the correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality review was performed where each QA pair was examined by a different annotator to verify: (i) language expression clarity and precision; (ii) question answerability with logically consistent options; (iii) appropriateness of the correct answer. Additionally, questions answerable by text alone (using Gemini 1.5 Pro) were filtered out. Certificate length analysis was conducted to analyze temporal difficulty of QA pairs, yielding median certificate lengths of 26s, 164.7s, and 890.7s for short, medium and long videos respectively. The distribution of options (A/B/C/D) follows a near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%), ensuring unbiased evaluation.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 questions per video (each with 4 candidate options)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning (expert annotators).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro (used to filter out QA pairs answerable without video content)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper identifies limitations in MLLMs' handling of longer video sequences, counting problems, action recognition, and temporal perception. Multilingual subtitles may have quality issues affecting evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Video-MME is designed as a benchmark for Testing/Evaluation of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on video understanding tasks. It evaluates perception, reasoning, and information synthesis capabilities across diverse video types, temporal durations, and data modalities (video frames, subtitles, and audio).
